sections.title: How to Calculate LIC Policy Maturity Value Online
sections.description: This calculator demystifies your LIC policy returns by applying the standard formula used for traditional endowment plans. Understand how LIC compares to other investment options with our FD vs PPF comparison and tax optimization guide. Here's the core logic:

content.text: Maturity Value = Basic Sum Assured + (Vested Bonus Ã— Policy Term) + Final Additional Bonus (FAB)

items: Basic Sum Assured (SA): The guaranteed amount you receive at maturity.

Vested Simple Reversionary Bonus: This is the bonus declared by LIC each year. It's calculated per â‚¹1,000 of your Sum Assured. For example, if the bonus rate is â‚¹42 and your SA is â‚¹10 Lakh, the bonus for that year is (10,00,000 / 1000) * 42 = â‚¹42,000. Our calculator multiplies this annual bonus by the policy term to find the total.

Final Additional Bonus (FAB): This is a one-time loyalty bonus paid at maturity for policies that have run for a long duration (typically 15+ years). It is also calculated per â‚¹1,000 SA and varies widely. You can input an illustrative rate, or leave it blank.

content.title: Key Assumptions
content.text:
• The bonus rates you enter are illustrative and assumed to remain constant for the entire policy term. Actual bonuses depend on LIC's performance and are not guaranteed.
  • GST paid on premiums is not included in the 'Total Premiums Paid' calculation, as it does not contribute to the maturity value.

In the unfortunate event of the policyholder's death during the policy term, the nominee receives the 'Sum Assured on Death' plus any vested bonuses. This 'Sum Assured on Death' is defined as the higher of:

content.title: Example
content.text: For a â‚¹10 Lakh policy with an annual premium of â‚¹50,000, the Sum Assured on Death would be the higher of â‚¹12.5 Lakh (125% of 10L) or â‚¹3.5 Lakh (7 x 50k), which is â‚¹12.5 Lakh, plus any accumulated bonuses.

If you stop paying premiums after at least two full years, your policy doesn't lapse completely. It becomes a 'paid-up' policy with reduced benefits. You don't have to pay any more premiums, and you will receive the 'Paid-up Sum Assured' plus vested bonuses at maturity.
Paid-up Value = Sum Assured Ã— (No. of Premiums Paid / Total Premiums Payable)

content.title: Example
content.text: If you have a 25-year policy with a â‚¹10 Lakh Sum Assured and a 16-year PPT, and you stop paying after 8 years, your Paid-up Sum Assured becomes: â‚¹10,00,000 * (8 / 16) = â‚¹5,00,000. This amount, plus bonuses accrued for 8 years, will be paid at maturity.

sections.title: Inputs Explained: What You Must Enter

items: Plan Preset: Selecting a specific plan like 'Jeevan Labh' helps the tool apply correct Premium Paying Terms (PPT) and typical bonus ranges. Explore our Jeevan Labh calculator, Jeevan Anand calculator, or other LIC plans for specific comparisons.

Premium & Term: The annual premium and the full policy term are needed to calculate total investment. Note the difference between Policy Term (e.g., 25 years) and Premium Paying Term (e.g., 16 years for Jeevan Labh).
Bonus & FAB Rates: The most critical inputs for an accurate estimate. You can find these in your annual policy statement or use the historical average of â‚¹40-â‚¹48 as a guideline.

Surrender/Loan Dates: Your Date of Birth and the date of the last premium paid are required to calculate the precise Surrender Value and loan eligibility. Use our LIC surrender value calculator for detailed analysis.

content.text:
Example 1: 30-Year-Old, â‚¹10 Lakh Cover, 25-Year Term

Inputs: SA = â‚¹10L, Term = 25 yrs, Annual Premium â‰ˆ â‚¹42,000, Bonus Rate = â‚¹45/1000, FAB Rate = â‚¹100/1000.

Calculation:
Maturity = 10,00,000 + ( (10,00,000/1000)*45*25 ) + ( (10,00,000/1000)*100 )
= 10,00,000 + 11,25,000 + 1,00,000 = â‚¹22,25,000
Approx. IRR: ~6.1% (tax-free)

Example 2: 35-Year-Old, â‚¹5 Lakh Cover, 15-Year Term

Inputs: SA = â‚¹5L, Term = 15 yrs, Annual Premium â‰ˆ â‚¹34,000, Bonus Rate = â‚¹40/1000.

Calculation:
Maturity = 5,00,000 + ( (5,00,000/1000)*40*15 )
= 5,00,000 + 3,00,000 = â‚¹8,00,000
Approx. IRR: ~5.8% (tax-free)

After paying premiums for at least 2 full years, your policy gains a 'Surrender Value'. This value is used to determine how much you get if you close the policy early, or how much you can borrow against it.

items: Guaranteed Surrender Value (GSV): A percentage of total premiums paid (e.g., 30% after 3 years) plus a percentage of vested bonuses. This is the minimum you'll receive.
Special Surrender Value (SSV): A higher, non-guaranteed value calculated by LIC, often closer to the real cash value. Our calculator estimates this.
Loan: You can typically borrow up to 90% of the Special Surrender Value.

content.text: Loan Calculation Example: If you've paid â‚¹2 Lakh in premiums over 5 years, your SSV might be around â‚¹1.5 Lakh. You could then take a loan of up to 90% of that, which is â‚¹1.35 Lakh.

items.q: How do I calculate my LIC policy maturity amount?
items.a: Enter sum assured, policy term, and an illustrative bonus rate per â‚¹1,000 SA into the calculator. Maturity = Sum Assured + (Vested bonus Ã— policy term) + Final Additional Bonus (if any). For other LIC plans, use our LIC premium calculator.

items.q: Does the LIC maturity calculator include bonus?
items.a: Yes. You can input an illustrative bonus rate per â‚¹1,000 SA or use historical averages. The calculator multiplies the annual bonus by the policy term to estimate total bonus.

items.q: How accurate is the maturity estimate?
items.a: Estimates use the inputs and illustrative bonus/FAB rates. Actual maturity depends on LIC's declared bonuses and final underwriting; treat results as indicative, not binding. Use our retirement corpus calculator for comprehensive retirement planning.

items.q: What is the formula for LIC maturity?
items.a: The formula is: Basic Sum Assured + Vested Simple Reversionary Bonuses + Final Additional Bonus (FAB). For comparisons, check our FD vs PPF calculator and PPF calculator.

items.q: What is Final Additional Bonus (FAB)?
items.a: FAB is a loyalty bonus paid by LIC at maturity on long-term participating policies. It is variable and declared by LIC depending on business performance.

items.q: How do I find the correct bonus rate to use?
items.a: Use the bonus rate shown on your policy statement or the published LIC bonus notifications. If unavailable, use a historical average (e.g., 40â€“48 per â‚¹1,000 SA for typical endowment plans).

items.q: Does GST affect my maturity?
items.a: No, GST is charged on the premium and does not affect the maturity calculation, which is based on Sum Assured and bonuses.

items.q: How is surrender value calculated for LIC policies?
items.a: Surrender value can be Guaranteed Surrender Value (a % of premiums paid) or Special Surrender Value (based on vested bonuses). Use our LIC surrender value calculator for precise estimates.

items.q: What is paid-up value?
items.a: Paid-up value applies if you stop paying premiums after two full years; benefits are reduced proportionately based on premiums paid and vested bonuses. The calculator can show paid-up estimates.

items.q: When can I take a loan on my LIC policy?
items.a: You can typically take a loan after the policy has acquired a surrender value, which is usually after paying premiums for 2-3 full years. Check our LIC surrender value calculator for loan eligibility.

items.q: Is LIC maturity tax-free under Section 10(10D)?
items.a: Generally yes, but the exemption depends on rules (notably if annual premium does not exceed 10% of Sum Assured for most policies). Check your policy specifics and use our tax regime calculator for tax planning.

items.q: What is modal loading?
items.a: Modal loading is the extra cost when paying premium monthly/quarterly/half-yearly versus yearly. The calculator converts yearly premium using modal factors to show accurate mode-wise premiums.

items.q: Can NRIs use this LIC maturity calculator?
items.a: Yes, NRIs can use the calculator for estimates. Actual purchase may be subject to FEMA and LIC rules for NRIs; check with LIC/agent for eligibility.

items.q: How do riders affect my premium and maturity?
items.a: Riders increase premium but do not increase the maturity sum-assured. Our calculator shows rider premium and the separate rider benefits (if any) but the maturity formula remains SA + bonuses + FAB.

items.q: How to calculate IRR on LIC policy?
items.a: IRR is the discount rate that equates total premiums paid with maturity received. Our calculator provides an approximate IRR after computing maturity and total premiums paid. Compare with PPF returns and FD returns.

items.q: Which LIC plans pay higher maturity?
items.a: Plans with longer terms and higher bonus rates (like Jeevan Labh's 25-year term) tend to yield higher maturity amounts due to longer compounding. Use our Jeevan Labh calculator to compare.

items.q: How to compare LIC maturity against FD/PPF?
items.a: Compare the post-tax IRR. LIC maturity is often tax-free, making its ~6% return equivalent to an 8-9% taxable return from an FD for someone in the 30% tax bracket. Use our FD vs PPF calculator for direct comparison.

items.q: Can I change Sum Assured during the policy?
items.a: No, the Basic Sum Assured is fixed at the time of policy issuance and cannot be changed during the term.

items.q: What happens if I stop paying premiums (paid-up)?
items.a: After 2 years, the policy can become 'paid-up' with a reduced Sum Assured. You won't have to pay more premiums, and you will receive the reduced sum assured plus vested bonuses at maturity.

items.q: How often does LIC declare bonus rates?
items.a: LIC declares its Simple Reversionary Bonus rates annually, typically after the end of each financial year (March 31st).
